extracted.intended_audience: petitioners and patent practitioners preparing inter partes review (IPR) petitions before the Patent Trial and Appeal Board (PTAB)
extracted.subtask_description: Checklist of required content and supporting showings that must be included in an IPR petition under 37 CFR § 42.104, including standing, identification of challenged claims, statutory grounds, claim construction, mapping to prior art, and supporting evidence. Intended to guide preparation of petitions seeking review of patent claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with other petition requirements (¶§ 42.6, 42.8, 42.22, 42.24)
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to the requirements of §§ 42.6, 42.8, 42.22, and 42.24, the petition must set forth the items listed in this section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Petitioner must ensure the petition also satisfies the procedural and content requirements found in those referenced sections (e.g., fee, service, pleadings format, and other filing requirements). Consult those sections for additional mandatory material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grounds for standing (certification of availability and no bar/estoppel)
rubrics_metrics.description: The petitioner must certify that the patent for which review is sought is available for inter partes review and that the petitioner is not barred or estopped from requesting an inter partes review challenging the patent claims on the grounds identified in the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include an explicit certification addressing availability of the patent for IPR and any potential procedural or equitable bars (such as prior settlements, earlier petitions, or estoppel issues). This is a jurisdictional/threshold requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statement of precise relief requested for each challenged claim
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide a statement of the precise relief requested for each claim challenged.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each claim the petition challenges, state plainly what you ask the Board to do (e.g., cancel claim 1 entirely, limit claim language, or find claim unpatentable). This overarching statement frames the subsequent detailed showings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of the claim (b)(1)
rubrics_metrics.description: Identify the claim (i.e., specify which patent claims are being challenged).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List claim numbers clearly and unambiguously so the Board and patent owner know exactly which claims are at issue. Where multiple claims are challenged, identify each separately.

rubrics_metrics.name: Specific statutory grounds and relied-upon patents/printed publications (b)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: State the specific statutory grounds under 35 U.S.C. 102 or 103 on which the challenge to the claim is based and the patents or printed publications relied upon for each ground.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For each challenged claim, tie the challenge to either anticipation (102) or obviousness (103) and identify the exact prior art references (patents or printed publications) relied upon for that ground. Be explicit which reference supports which ground for which claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim construction and 35 U.S.C. 112(f) identification (b)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the challenged claim is to be construed. Where the claim contains a means-plus-function or step-plus-function limitation under 35 U.S.C. 112(f), the construction must identify the specific portions of the specification that describe the structure, material, or acts corresponding to each claimed function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide proposed constructions of claim terms/limitations relied on in the challenge. If asserting 112(f) limitations, explicitly point to the portions of the specification that disclose corresponding structure/material/acts. Make constructions clear because the unpatentability analysis depends on them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Showing how the construed claim is unpatentable and element-by-element mapping (b)(4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain how the construed claim is unpatentable under the statutory grounds identified in paragraph (b)(2). The petition must specify where each element of the claim is found in the prior art patents or printed publications relied upon.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an element-by-element comparison mapping each claim limitation (as construed) to specific disclosures in the prior art references (or explain combination/reasoning for 103). Make the linkage explicit rather than conclusory to allow the Board to assess the merits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exhibit identification and statement of relevance (b)(5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide the exhibit number of the supporting evidence relied upon to support the challenge and the relevance of the evidence to the challenge raised, including identifying specific portions of the evidence that support the challenge.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cite exhibit numbers and point to precise pages/portions of exhibits that corroborate factual or technical assertions. The Board may exclude or give no weight to evidence where a party has failed to state its relevance or to identify specific portions of the evidence that support the challenge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion to correct clerical or typographical mistakes (c)
rubrics_metrics.description: A motion may be filed that seeks to correct a clerical or typographical mistake in the petition. The grant of such a motion does not change the filing date of the petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If minor clerical/typographical errors are discovered after filing, a corrective motion is available, but petitioners should not expect the petition's filing date to be altered by such corrections (important for timeliness/priority).
